body: 14 Nov 2026 00:45 UTC, ROOT CAUSE PROVEN on the bench (emulator, debug build 150 of main dbe63d0, fresh sign-in as the test account on VM 108 updated to image sha-7c7fa60; engineering check, NOT the release-candidate pair). Phone: 3,387 live track rows at sign-in +73 s, ALL is_ref=1 (0 old-style music-server rows), and 178 files (file_id) are held by 2 or 3 live rows each (e.g. 'From Can to Can't': ref with the artists list and a cover + ref with ONE joined artist string and no cover; 'Hate Me' by Blue October: album None + album '[Unknown Album]'; 'Darkbloom': three refs). So it is NOT leftover rows of the old mode and NOT release-candidate row B1/F30 (the samples labelled +0 s and +60 s were really taken at about +73 s because the scheduled times had already passed; the +180 s sample shows the same 178). SERVER: the same 178 navidrome songs are attached to more than one song_ref (server/encore_server/encore_server, read-only query on the VM's database): 176 are 'youtube then library' and 2 are 'youtube then youtube'. Mechanism (read in scanner.py link_library + refs.py find/resolve/attach_file): the KEEPER attaches the saved file to the ref the import made (source youtube); LATER the library scan describes the same file from its TAGS, refs.find misses it (the tags carry the artists as one joined string so artists[0] and norm_key differ [audit B-119, old keeper tags]; or the duration differs by 1 to 12 s beyond _compatible; or the album is '[Unknown Album]'), refs.resolve makes a NEW ref and attach_file attaches the same navidrome_song_id to it. 695 playlist entries of the test account point at refs of such files. PLAN decided by the advisor: A (small, now): link_library looks the file up across all refs by navidrome_song_id OR path BEFORE describing it from tags, uses the owning ref and creates nothing (helper-n11a, PR to come; the 2 'youtube then youtube' cases are another cause, audit B-110, not fixed by A). B (repair of the existing 178): merge ONLY refs that share a file (never on norm_key: 73 collisions may be different versions), survivor = the first-attached ref, never copy '[Unknown Album]' onto the survivor, re-point likes, playlist entries, history, downloads and the saved queue BEFORE deleting a loser; two checks first: (1) what the phone does when a ref it holds is merged away (do NOT reuse encore_upgrade._rekey: its UPDATE OR IGNORE skips a row whenever the new id already exists, which is the merge case); (2) a dry run on a copy of the VM's database (duplicates 178 to 0, like and playlist-entry counts unchanged, no row pointing at a deleted ref). B is NOT deployed to VM 108 before the dry run passes: VM 108 is the server the owner's A35 uses. The gap found while building N-24: a song by several artists on another artist's album is not linked to that artist (B-118).
